steps.intro: Mark each line Holds or Fails. A note on any of them is welcome.

steps.headline: This is a second option to compare against the layout you already approved. Neither is chosen yet.
steps.changed: I build it as a switch in the practice app, beside the approved layout, so you can click through both. The real app does not change.
steps.notice: You end up with two clickable versions side by side and pick one, or mix them.

steps.headline: The three-line menu and the session name become one button on the left.
steps.changed: There is no separate three-line button and no session dropdown. Tapping the name opens the new full-screen menu.
steps.notice: One tap target on the left instead of two. The name stops being centred and starts right after the menu icon.

steps.headline: The status dots move to the left, lined up with the start of the menu icon and name.
steps.changed: Today's approved design centres the dots under a centred name. Here they start at the left edge of the combined button.
steps.notice: The dots read as part of the menu button rather than floating in the middle.
steps.resolved: Built that way: the lights stay under the name, right of the menu icon, starting at the name's left edge instead of centred.

steps.headline: Session files gets its own button again, beside the terminal switch, with no number on it.
steps.changed: Today on a phone, Session files is a row in the three-line menu showing a count, like "Session files (3)". Here it is a button at top right, icon only.
steps.notice: Files for this chat are one tap away instead of two. You no longer see how many there are until you open it.

steps.path: Tap the name at top left
steps.headline: The menu fills the screen: New session at the top, then Active sessions, then Previous sessions.
steps.changed: This replaces both today's three-line menu and the session dropdown. It works like the ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini phone apps: one list of every chat, open ones first.
steps.notice: Everything about chats is in one place, and past chats are visible without asking for them.

steps.headline: On a phone there is no separate Resume button. Tapping a past chat reopens it.
steps.changed: Today you press Resume to open a separate page of past chats, then pick one. Here past chats are already listed in the menu.
steps.notice: Reopening a past chat takes one tap from the menu instead of two plus a page.
steps.resolved: Your worry about when a past chat counts as reopened, and keeping the X to end a chat, is now its own question on the design page.

steps.path: The New session button at the top
steps.headline: New session still opens the full form, with every option it has today.
steps.changed: Folder, model, permissions and the rest stay. Only where the form appears changes, to fit the full-screen menu.
steps.notice: Nothing you can set when starting a chat goes away.

steps.headline: Projects, Pages, Browser and Games move into this menu too.
steps.changed: Today they are rows in the three-line menu with Settings and Session files. Here they sit in the full-screen menu, and Session files leaves for the top bar.
steps.notice: The menu becomes the one place for everything that is not the chat itself.
steps.resolved: Browser now sits at top right beside Session files. Only Projects, Pages and Games moved into the menu.

steps.headline: Settings is its own button at the bottom and opens today's full-screen Settings page.
steps.changed: On a phone, Settings already opens as a full-screen page. The only change is reaching it from a button at the foot of the new menu.
steps.notice: Settings stays where your thumb rests, like the phone apps you named.

steps.path: Under the message box, and session rows everywhere
steps.headline: The pills, shortcut chips and model-only rows you approved stay the same in this alternative.
steps.changed: Only the top bar and the menus differ between the two options.
steps.notice: Comparing the two means comparing the top and the menu, nothing else.

steps.intro: Who gets it, and what happens to things the Resume page does today.

steps.headline: Should the alternative also apply to a narrow computer window, or only to phones?
steps.today: The layout you approved applies whenever the screen is narrow, phone or computer window alike.
steps.checked: Read in the branch's top-bar code on 2026-11-27: the narrow layout follows screen width, not device.
steps.problem: A full-screen menu on a computer window would hide the chat entirely while open, which a computer user may not expect.
steps.proposal: Draw it for phones first, and decide the narrow computer window once you have seen it.

options.label: Phones only
options.summary: A narrow computer window keeps the approved layout.
pros: A computer window keeps a small menu that does not cover the chat.
cons: Phone and narrow computer window would look different from each other.

options.label: Phones and windows
options.summary: Any narrow screen gets the full-screen menu.
cons: The menu covers the whole window on a computer, too.

steps.headline: With Resume gone on phones, how do you find an old chat that is far down the list?
steps.today: The Resume page has a search box and can be narrowed to one project folder. It lists every past chat.
steps.checked: Read in the app's Resume page code on master on 2026-11-27.
steps.problem: A plain list in a menu has neither. Finding a chat from last month would mean a lot of scrolling.
steps.proposal: Put a search box at the top of the menu, as the ChatGPT and Claude phone apps do.

options.label: Search in menu
options.summary: A search box at the top of the menu filters every chat, open and past.
pros: Any chat is a few letters away.
Matches the phone apps you named.
cons: One more thing at the top of the menu.

options.label: See all link
options.summary: The menu lists recent chats; a See all row at the end opens today's Resume page with its search.
pros: Keeps search and project filtering exactly as today.
cons: The Resume page lives on, just reached differently.

options.label: List only
cons: No way to search past chats on a phone.

steps.headline: Anything about how you picture these screens before I draw them? Skip if not.
steps.prompt: e.g. groups by date, big New session button, icons along the bottom…
steps.today: You have described the order: New session, Active sessions, Previous sessions, other places, Settings at the bottom.
steps.problem: I will draw two to four versions of the menu and the top bar next; a picture in your head saves a round.
steps.proposal: Write anything you already see. Leave it blank and I draw from your message alone.
steps.resolved: Kept as a later idea, letting each person pick their own layout. Nothing is built for it in this round.

steps.intro: Reworked from your notes. Say if the top bar and menu are right now, and answer the two new questions.

steps.headline: Is the top bar right now?
steps.reopened: You asked for this chat's light under the name in a ring, much tighter spacing, and no dot on the menu icon.
steps.caption: The reworked top bar, in the practice app.
steps.today: The first drawing had a dot before the name, the lights hanging well below it, and a warning dot on the menu icon.
steps.checked: Rebuilt and photographed in the practice app on 2026-11-28.
steps.problem: The name and lights read as two loose pieces, and the dot before the name repeated what the lights show.
steps.proposal: No dot before the name. This chat's light sits in the row under it, in its strip order, inside a thin ring. The lights start under the name's first letter, right below it, and the pair is centred on the menu icon.

from: the ring idea from the selected pill in the wide session switcher
reuse.note: The menu icon's warning dot moved to the Settings tile in the menu.

steps.path: Tap the name at top left
steps.headline: Is the redrawn menu right?
steps.reopened: You picked tiles, and asked for the guide's look: no lines, clearer buttons, a header like other screens, Settings and pinned pages as tiles.
steps.caption: The redrawn menu, in the practice app.
steps.today: The first drawing had a search box at the very top, a line above the places, borderless icons, and Settings as a wide button at the bottom.
steps.checked: Read the design guide's Spacing, Buttons, Full screens and Lists sections, and photographed phone Settings and Pages for reference, on 2026-11-28.
steps.problem: It did not look like the app's other phone screens, and the places did not read as buttons.
steps.proposal: A Chats title at left and a close button at right, like phone Settings. Then search and New session. At the foot, one row of boxed tiles: Settings, Projects, Pages, Games, then each pinned page. It slides sideways under a soft fade when it does not fit. No lines anywhere; space separates the parts.

reuse.note: Session rows stay plain rows, as the guide asks for switchers.

steps.path: Tap a chat under Previous sessions
steps.headline: When you tap a past chat in the menu, what should happen?
steps.today: Picking a chat on the Resume page restarts it straight away; it joins your open sessions at once, and some chats first ask which model to use.
steps.checked: Read in the app's Resume page and session code on master on 2026-11-28. The Resume page already has a read-only preview of a past chat.
steps.problem: In a menu you scroll through, a tap that restarts the chat would turn every quick look into an open session you then have to close with its X.
steps.proposal: A tap opens the chat to read. It only becomes an active session, and only asks for a model, when you send a message.

options.label: Read, then send
options.summary: The chat opens to read; sending a message restarts it.
pros: Looking back never leaves an extra open chat.
Matches the phone apps you named.
cons: New work: the read-only view needs a message box.

options.label: Reopen at once
options.summary: A tap restarts the chat, as Resume does today.
pros: Works the way it does now; little new work.
cons: Every look adds an open session you must end with its X.

steps.path: Tap a tile at the foot of the menu
steps.headline: When you tap a tile, should the menu fade into that screen, or stay and change in place?
steps.today: In the practice app, a tap fades the menu's title to the tile's name, opens that screen underneath, and fades the menu away over it in about a fifth of a second.
steps.checked: Built in the practice app on 2026-11-28; a fade cannot be shown in a still picture.
steps.problem: Your note asked for the title and the right page to fade in when one is picked. It could mean either of two things, and they work very differently.
steps.proposal: Keep the fade into the screen: every screen still opens and closes the way it does today.

options.label: Fade into the screen
options.summary: The title changes, then the menu fades away and leaves you on that screen.
pros: Screens open and close as today.
cons: The menu closes each time; coming back means opening it again.

options.label: Change in place
options.summary: The menu stays open; the tiles act like tabs, and the area above them fades to that screen.
pros: Jumping between places never leaves the menu.
cons: Every screen must fit inside the menu: a lot of new work.
Two ways to reach each screen.

steps.path: A warning, like a failing backup
steps.headline: With no dot on the menu icon, where should a warning show while the menu is closed?
steps.today: Today a failing backup or a waiting game challenge puts a dot on the menu icon. In this version, as you asked, it sits only on the Settings or Games tile inside the menu.
steps.checked: Read in the menu icon's code on the branch, 2026-11-28.
steps.problem: Someone who never opens the menu would not learn that their backup is failing.
steps.proposal: Keep it on the tile only, as you asked, and decide again once you have used it.

options.label: Tile only
options.summary: The dot shows only on its tile in the menu.
cons: A warning waits until the menu is opened.

options.label: Also on the bar
options.summary: A small dot at the end of the lights row too, while something needs you.
pros: A warning is seen without opening anything.
cons: The bar carries a second kind of dot.
